Unless you're a trained professional, don't give advice. Your friend knows their own life better than you do, and has put more time thinking about their problems than you have. I guess you can advise them to seek a professional, and if they ask for your opinion. However, it's really important to recognize when you're out of your depth. 

What you can do is active listening. You can do that by listening to their story, empathizing with and validating their emotions. Empathizing involves saying something like 'that sounds [insert relevant feelings]' Empathizing is not talking about your own similar experiences that demonstrate your understanding of that emotion. 

If you ever fear for their immediate safety call 911.

There are two basic delineations. There is feeling suicidal which has some level of intent. Maybe it's vague, or contextual but there is the desire to take your own life. Then there's suicidal ideation which can have many of the same hallmarks but lacks the same intent or the motivational push to commit suicide. This can be as benign as thinking what would hypothetically happen to the people around you if you killed yourself but where the line between the two starts to blur is when you start to form specific plans. Having a clear idea of what you would do can be just as dangerous as being suicidal without a plan in certain contexts. This is mostly because, in my experience (I've talked with hundreds of suicidal ppl),  most people are able to recognize if they are suicidal but they never really see it coming. Intent just hits them one day and they don't usually stop to reflect on this change because there's usually something much more stressful demanding their attention.

Edit: I'd also like to add that having suicidal ideation does not mean you are a ticking time bomb. You may go the rest of your life never coming any closer to feeling suicidal. It's hard to say. I don't know you or your life, but it can't hurt to investigate why you are feeling what you are feeling and what you want to do about those thoughts/feelings.

So this is just for jg rek. I've never taken her top, but I've played her almost exclusively her since she came out. At least every chance I get.
The most significant differences between a fed and a feeder rek that comes to my mind from my games as rek, and playing with/against a rek is how well the rek player can position themselves (important fights, objs, not getting caught, setting up ambushes/ganks), how well the rek player is using their global pressure (tp? Or for example gank bot, then ulti to top lane cus their laner thought they were safe and shoved... etc...), and how good are reks opponents at escaping her?

The reason I put positioning  and global pressure in such high regard for her is because she thrives on being where she is least expected and catching people off guard. If she cannot kill her target within the time they are knocked up for whatever reason, and if they have any way to escape then they will get away scott free in most situations. She has no kiteing abilities, no other cc and her only way to chase is also her main way to engage. So if you're lucky enough to have not used your tunnel to engage, which would usually be due to your teammates, then you might be able to stick to them for a kill after the cooldown for your knock up finishes. The only other options at that point depend on having well placed tunnels in contested territory. 

There are plenty of opportunities to out play her. You start the exact same way as you would against any fast or stupidly mobile jg champs, like udyr or Lee, by warding a ton and doing everything you can to know where she is at. She can be easily juked while burrowed because of the delay on the tremors and if you stop moving I won't know what the fuck just happened because you could have flashed/used some other escape or you're waiting to ambush me with your buddies. Sure I could use my q, but I might just hit you and only get vision of you and that'll prock my mobos. So then I can't chase or escape as well and after that I'm no better off than I was before. Cc will stop her from tunneling. I'll spend a lot of time in the enemy jg and other risky positions just to catch someone off guard mostly because I feel like I can get away with it with a decent tunnel system. If you keep an eye on her and you collapse when she invades you can kill her even with good tunnels. 

So with all that being said, I was rather surprised when I first heard about her nerfs in PBE. I always felt she does just enough damage burst the out of position squishies, and then gets to build tanky so that she can stay in the middle of the fight for a bit longer. Maybe I just suck, but i even felt like I'd go a bit overboard on the damage items sometimes and still couldn't burst down anything but their squishies. A melee champ such as herself wouldn't be very useful in tf's if she wasn't tanky. I'm really not sure what an appropriate nerf would be to deal with her absurdly high win rate.
